This appeal is filed at the instance of the claimant in O.P.(MV) No.719 of 2017 and seeks to challenge the award dated 15.01.2021 of the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Thodupuzha.
The accident occurred on 26.05.2017 when the claimant was aged 50 years.

2. I have heard Sri.P.C. Haridas, the learned counsel for the appellant, as well as Sri.M. Premchand,
the learned counsel for the Insurance Company.
3. The first issue that arises for consideration is as regards the fixation of the notional income by the Tribunal at Rs.10,000/-.
The claimant had pointed out that he, being an agriculturist, was earning a monthly income of Rs.15,000/-.
At the same time, insofar as the claimant did not adduce any evidence in support of the income claimed, the Tribunal estimated the same at Rs.10,000/-.

At the same time, with reference to an accident of the year 2017, the notional income requires to be fixed at Rs.11,000/-, with reference to the principles laid down by the Apex Court in Ramachandrappa V.
Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Company Ltd. [(2011) 13 SCC 236].

Ramachandrappa V.
Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Company Ltd. [(2011) 13 SCC 236]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The award of the Tribunal requires to be modified to that extent, and I do so.

4. The second issue arising for consideration is as regards the disability quantified at 14% by the Tribunal on the face of the disability 2025:KER:93570 certificate issued by the Medical Board as evidenced by Ext.A10 at 24 percentage.
In paragraph 16 of the impugned award, the Tribunal found that, considering the job of the claimant as an agriculturist, the functional disability only requires to be quantified at 14%.

At the same time, considering the nature of the injuries as noticed by the Tribunal with reference to the certification by the Medical Board in paragraph 16 and more particularly, the nature of the injuries noticed in paragraph 9 of the impugned award, I am of the opinion that if the case of the claimant that he is an agriculturalist is being acted upon, the Tribunal ought to have fixed the functional disability at 24% as quantified by the Medical Board.
This is especially so when the said certificate is issued not by an individual doctor but by a Board attached to the District Hospital, Thodupuzha.
In such circumstances, the award of the Tribunal requires to be modified to that extent, and I do so.
5. The last issue arising for consideration is with reference to the awarding of compensation only for a period of three months under the head 'Loss of earnings'.
I notice that the claimant had serious injuries, as noticed in paragraph 9 of the impugned award, as well as the nature of the injuries certified by Ext.A10.

In the light of the nature of injuries as noticed in paragraph 9 of the impugned award, especially the fracture of as many as six ribs, I am of the opinion that the claimant will be entitled 2025:KER:93570 to compensation under the head "Loss of earnings" for a period of eight months.
Subject to the aforementioned modifications, the award of the Tribunal is sustained.
